title: Both of Skybase's emergency response protocols are deferred, while its emergency governance powers are already in force
content:
A.6.1.1.4.3.1.3 (Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response) and A.6.1.1.4.3.1.4 (Agent-Specific Emergency Response) both consist of a single sentence: the protocol "will be specified in a future iteration of the Skybase Artifact." The Artifact distinguishes the two cases — situations affecting the whole ecosystem versus situations affecting only Skybase — and then defines neither.

Meanwhile every Instance in the Artifact carries an Emergency Protocol document, and A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 already grants the Operational Facilitator a live power: in an Urgent or Emergency Situation they "may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above," with public announcement owed only where feasible and excusable if disclosure would endanger Skybase or its users.

So the *authority* to act fast in an emergency exists now, while the *procedure* the Agent will follow, and the criteria distinguishing an ecosystem-wide from an Agent-specific event, do not. The compressed-timeline power is bounded by a Core Atlas definition of emergency situations, but nothing in Skybase's own Artifact says what Skybase does when one occurs.

This is the deferral pattern seen throughout — Genesis Supply, token address, partner payment addresses, tracking methodologies — appearing in the one area where improvisation is least acceptable. Elsewhere a missing parameter delays a payment; here a missing protocol is filled in under time pressure by whoever holds the emergency power.

The structural mitigation is that the placeholders exist and are addressable, so the gap is disclosed rather than latent, and filling them is a Root Edit against a named document rather than a new drafting exercise.
description: Ecosystem-wide and Agent-specific emergency response are each 'to be specified in a future iteration', though the emergency Root Edit path lets the Facilitator compress timelines today.
